en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Fourteenth Chapter
On the Discussion of the Indeterminate: Is the range of views indeterminate? Yes.
Is matter that is indeterminate as result (vipākābyākata) or indeterminate as functional (kriyābyākata), Nibbāna,
the eye-base …pe… and the tangible-object-base?
One should not say so …pe…
Is the state of views indeterminate? Yes.
Is contact associated with the state of views indeterminate?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … Is a speculative view indeterminate? Yes.
Feeling associated with views … perception … volition … [and so forth] … [as above].
Is consciousness indeterminate?
One should not say so… [as before] … Is contact associated with a speculative view unwholesome?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is a speculative view unwholesome?
You should not say so …pe…
Is feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness associated with a state of view unwholesome?
Yes. Is a state of view unwholesome?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is a speculative view indeterminate? Yes.
“Is it fruitless and without ripening?
“One should not say so.
…pe… “Is it not rather fruitful and with ripening?”
“Yes.
“If it is with fruit and with result, then indeed, sir, you should not say:
‘A speculative view is indeterminate.’”
Is the state of views indeterminate? Yes.
But has it not been said by the Blessed One that wrong view is the foremost of faults?
“Yes.
“If it is true that the Blessed One has stated that faults have wrong view as their supreme [evil], then surely you should not say:
‘A speculative view is undeclared (avyākata).’”
Is a speculative view indeterminate?
Yes. But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“Wrong view, Vaccha, is unwholesome; right view is wholesome.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
In that case, it should not be said that "a speculative view is indeterminate.
Is a speculative view indeterminate?
“Yes, [it is so].
“Is it not stated by the Blessed One:
‘Punna, for one of wrong view, I declare one of two destinations: either hell or the animal realm’?”
“Or to hell, or to the animal realm.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, it should not be said that "a speculative view is indeterminate.
It should not be said [that way].
“Is a speculative view indeterminate?”— Yes.
But was it not said by the Blessed One:
“‘The world is eternal,’ Vaccha, this has not been declared by me;
‘the world is not eternal,’ Vaccha, this has not been declared by me;
‘the world is finite,’ Vaccha, this has not been declared by me.”
‘The world is infinite,’ Vaccha …pe… ‘The soul and the body are the same,’ Vaccha …pe… ‘The soul is one thing and the body another,’ Vaccha …pe…
‘The Tathāgata exists after death,’ Vaccha, ...
[as before] ... ‘The Tathāgata does not exist after death,’ Vaccha, ...
[as before] ... ‘The Tathāgata both exists and does not exist after death,’ Vaccha, ... [as before] ...
“‘Whether the Tathāgata exists after death, or does not exist, or both, or neither’—this, Vaccha, has been left undeclared by me.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
"Therefore, the speculative view is indeterminate.
"Is the speculative view indeterminate?
"Yes."
Has it not been said by the Blessed One:
“Bhikkhus, for a person of wrong view, whatever bodily action he undertakes in accordance with that view, whatever verbal action...
whatever mental action, whatever volition, and whatever aspiration—”
“And whatever aspiration there is, and whatever volitional formations there are— all those phenomena lead to what is unwished for, undesired, unpleasant, unbeneficial, and suffering.
Is this indeed a sutta?
“Yes, [it is].
In that case, it should not be said that “a speculative view is indeterminate.”
The Discussion on the Indeterminate is finished.
